note: Both bounds appear with the same exponents, the remainder one in the algebra norm and in every viewer; the Lean threshold is an eventual statement in r. The Lean also concludes injectivity of the position lists, so it states more.

snippet.text: lemma coefficient_separated (m:ℕ)(j:R.channels m): ∀ᶠ r:ℝ in 𝓝[>] 0,∀ (x':I→ E4)(o':E4), WithinRoom r M η x' o' → ‖R.coef m j x' v o'‖ ≤ r^((m:ℝ)-weight d-ε) := by

proof_context.conclusion: Eventually as r tends to 0 from above, every `WithinRoom` configuration has `||R.coef m j x v o|| <= r^(m - weight d - eps)`.

snippet.text:
lemma quantitative_separated (D:ℕ)(hδ:0<δ) :∀ᶠ r:ℝ in 𝓝[>] 0,∀ (x:I→E4)(o:E4)(y:J→E4), WithinRoom r M η x o → ClearOf o y δ →
   Injective (beside x y) ∧ Injective (beside (sole o) y) ∧
      ‖algebraError U R x o v y w D‖≤ r^((D:ℝ)+1 - weight d-ε) ∧ ∀ t:Viewers U,‖formula U R x o v y w D t‖≤ r^((D:ℝ)+1-weight d-ε):=by

proof_context.conclusion: Eventually in r, for `WithinRoom` and `ClearOf` configurations the point lists are injective, `||algebraError|| <= r^(D+1 - weight d - eps)` and every viewer value of `formula` obeys the same bound.
